items.title: The AI Riemann hypothesis proof is true, independent mathematicians confirm
items.excerpt: Independent mathematicians have checked the AI-assisted (Claude/Lean) proof of the Riemann hypothesis claimed by Anthropic's Levent Alpöge and report it is almost certainly correct, the first outside verification of the claim covered 11-21.

history_match.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to prove Riemann hypothesis, most famous problem in all of math

items.title: The Communal Brain Behind RFD4-Proteina
items.excerpt: Baker's IPD and NVIDIA release RFD4-Proteina, a generative protein-design model merging RoseTTAFold Diffusion and Proteina-Complexa that yields 5-10x more high-quality designs than prior methods, with wet-lab validation loops; R&D World reports it designed a pesticide-degrading enzyme.
items.subtopic: life_science (de novo protein/enzyme design model release)

history_match.title: Nvidia, UW Institute for Protein Design unveil open-source protein design AI model

items.title: Scientists Use AI-Designed CRISPR to Make Disease-Resistant Rice
items.excerpt: University of Missouri team (Bing Yang) adapted Profluent's AI-designed gene editor OpenCRISPR-1 for rice, editing three SWEET genes with up to 97% efficiency; edited plants resisted three Xoo blight strains and passed edits to offspring.

history_match.title: Rice plants can fight off devastating disease after gene editing with AI-designed tool

items.title: Milky Way simulation reaches record resolution with the help of three supercomputers
items.excerpt: University of Tokyo/RIKEN (Keiya Hirashima) simulated the Milky Way star by star across three supercomputers, using an AI model to predict supernova gas evolution so the galaxy simulation takes longer time steps and runs ~20x faster (SC 2026).

items.title: Putting Google's AI hurricane model to the test
items.excerpt: UAlbany study of 385 tropical cyclones (Geophysical Research Letters) finds Google's WeatherNext Cyclone beat NOAA's hurricane model on intensity at 1-5 days and matched human forecasters, but underestimated strength and gave too-narrow uncertainty ranges.
items.subtopic: physics/earth (independent evaluation of AI weather model; weather emulators deprioritized)

items.title: AI and experiments reveal impurities hindering waste plastic pyrolysis oil recycling
items.excerpt: KRICT and KOREATECH combined a machine-learning potential with experiments (ACS Catalysis) to show nitrogen impurities such as 2-methylpyridine occupy zeolite catalyst sites first and cut light-olefin yields in plastic pyrolysis-oil upcycling.

items.title: AI guardrails falter as tampering drives repeated harassment in simulated conversations
items.excerpt: Georgia State, Georgia Tech and UC Berkeley tested Gemini, Llama, Qwen and DeepSeek agents in multi-turn simulated chats; toxic memory, planning prompts or fine-tuning pushed harassment rates as high as 97% and hostility escalated over turns (ICWSM).

items.title: Electron fingerprints help AI predict complex alloy properties with little training data
items.excerpt: Sandia, Georgia Tech and NASA's VASt model identifies high-entropy alloys by electron distribution rather than composition, predicting heat and stress response from a few dozen samples (npj Computational Materials).
items.subtopic: materials (alloys; note paper from June, data-efficiency method)

history_match.title: Chat-based AI lets users run complex alloy calculations on their own computers

items.title: Noninvasive brain interface uses AI suggestions to convey messages nearly three times faster
items.excerpt: Rutgers' ChatBCI-Assist pairs an EEG P300 speller with a locally run fine-tuned language model that suggests words and phrases, nearly tripling meaning-based spelling speed in healthy participants (IEEE TBME).

items.title: New research calls for stronger standards when using LLMs and other AI tools for psychological assessment
items.excerpt: Child Mind Institute, Harvard and MIT researchers (PLOS Digital Health) show AI language tools can score well overall yet miss less common symptom expressions, and propose a 'Text Psychometrics' validation framework for LLM-based psychological assessment.

items.title: People prefer AI to human advice in multi-turn conversations but neither changes incentivised behaviour
items.excerpt: Maier, Lieder, Cheung et al. ran a donation-decision experiment where participants chatted with an LLM advisor, a human, or no one: LLM advisors were judged more rational, trustworthy, convincing and sycophantic, yet donations did not differ across conditions.

items.title: Collisionality scaling of the tokamak density limit
items.excerpt: MIT PSFC-led team (Maris, Rea et al.) used machine-learning-guided analysis of a multi-machine database (C-Mod, ASDEX Upgrade, DIII-D, JET, TCV) to find a common edge-collisionality threshold for density-limit disruptions with far fewer false positives than the Greenwald limit.

items.title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
items.excerpt: Harvard's Chenyang Jin, Susanne Yelin and Andi Gu introduce Rapids, a streaming neural decoder co-designed with an FPGA that is both fast enough for superconducting syndrome cycles and accurate, cutting the qubit overhead of real-time error correction.

history_match.title: Yonsei University Researchers Develop Mamba State-Space Neural Decoder to Enable Real-Time Quantum Error Correction

items.title: Supervised deep learning for efficient cryo-EM image alignment in drug discovery with cryoPARES
items.excerpt: cryoPARES is a supervised deep-learning framework that reuses prior alignments to rapidly determine particle poses across closely related cryo-EM datasets, speeding structure determination for ligand series.

items.title: A quantitative deep-learning-based framework reveals a continuum of chromatin sensitivities across transcription factors
items.excerpt: A deep-learning framework shows transcription-factor binding sensitivity to chromatin is a continuum rather than binary, with binding explained by a mix of hierarchical and cooperative mechanisms.

items.title: Enabling lab autonomy with reward functions and executable workflows
items.excerpt: Kalinin et al. argue self-driving labs need LLM hypothesis generation complemented by bottom-up optimization that turns hypotheses into executable workflows with explicit reward functions (Perspective).

items.title: New AI 'copilot' helps engineers design better structures
items.excerpt: MIT researchers built a human-in-the-loop topology-optimization 'copilot' that presents regions of a structure to the designer for feedback while the algorithm generates it.
